Subject: Sizing check: dedicated commit for Pinegrove pilot

Hi Camila / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Pinegrove liked the latency profile and the ability to pin model versions. Before we tee up commercial terms, can you help validate a sizing sketch so we can align procurement? High level:
- Workload: single-turn summarization + short Q&A (avg output 45 tokens, avg input 120 tokens)
- Expected steady-state: ~1M tokens/day (customer estimate)
- Peak concurrency: observed spikes up to ~220 tokens/sec in internal tests (30-minute bursts)
- SLO target: p95 end-to-end latency < 200 ms for short summaries; p95 < 400 ms for Q&A OK

Questions:
1) Rough tokens/sec (TPS) to GPU mapping for the model variants we discussed (Redwood-optimized 70B float16, 70B quantized, 13B quantized).
2) How much headroom you recommend for bursts and cold-starts (percentage).
3) If we commit to a 3-month pilot reserved slab, what slab size would you recommend to hit the SLOs above with autoscale to handle peaks?

Attaching a sampled workload profile (CSV) — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Regards,
Samir Patel
VP Engineering, Pinegrove AI

Samir — thanks for the profile, this is exactly what we need to start a concrete sizing. Initial, quick answers below and I looped in Karthik for a tighter model-by-model run. Ben — adding you for pricing/commit context.

Quick take (high level):
- TPS per GPU (back-of-envelope):
  * Redwood-optimized 70B float16 (H100 class): ~55–75 TPS (1-token generation throughput for typical short summaries).
  * 70B quantized (4-bit, Redwood q4): ~100–140 TPS.
  * 13B quantized (q4): ~250–320 TPS.
- Headroom: recommend target steady utilization of ~60–70% per slab to account for burstiness and tail-latency variance — i.e., ~30–40% headroom.
- Pilot slab: based on your 1M tokens/day and the observed 220 TPS short bursts, a 4-GPU reserved slab (quantized 70B or mix with 13B for lower-latency paths) should cover steady loads with autoscale to 8 GPUs for sustained peaks. This assumes prefix caching and request batching are enabled.

Next steps: Karthik will share a short table mapping your CSV profile to per-model TPS and an inline spreadsheet with the math. If that looks good we can convert to a mutual action plan and lock a pilot commit. Attaching an initial sizing workbook I used as a template.

- Camila Reyes

Samir / Camila / Ben,

I mapped the workload sample to per-model throughput and built a small sensitivity table — pasted summary below and attached a CSV with the full rows. Key assumptions: avg output 45 tokens, avg input 120 tokens, batching latency budget 10–30 ms, KV cache hit rate 12% (warm sessions).

Summary (typical TPS numbers for single-token generation, measured under Redwood runtime):
- 70B float16 (H100 profile): ~65 TPS per GPU (p50); p95 tail ~40 TPS due to headroom for attention overheads.
- 70B q4: ~120 TPS per GPU (p50); p95 ~75 TPS.
- 13B q4: ~300 TPS per GPU (p50); p95 ~180 TPS.

Pilot sizing math (rounded):
- Steady-state tokens/day -> 1,000,000 tokens/day => avg token/sec ≈ 11.6 TPS sustained.
- But your observed 30-min bursts hit 220 TPS.

If Pinegrove commits to using 70B q4 for quality parity, plan:
- Reserve slab: 4 GPUs (each ~120 TPS p50) => nominal capacity ~480 TPS p50. With 30% headroom target, usable steady capacity ~336 TPS. That covers 220 TPS peaks with margin.
- Autoscale floor/ceiling: floor 2 GPUs for quiet hours, ceiling 8 GPUs for sustained peaks (8x120 = 960 TPS).

If Pinegrove prefers a hybrid to improve p95 latency:
- Mix: 2x 70B q4 + 2x 13B q4 => combined p50 ~ (2*120 + 2*300) = 840 TPS p50. This delivers lower-latency routing for short summaries and keeps quality-critical completions on 70B.

Recommendations and caveats:
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeat context-heavy traffic (reduces effective TPS by ~10–20%).
- Configure request batching to maintain sub-200ms p95 — aggressive batching hurts p95 for short requests, so cap batching window at 12 ms for summary path.
- Reserve additional 20–30% capacity during initial 2-week ramp to monitor tail-latency and hot partitions.

I attached the detailed model_tps_table.csv with per-prompt bucket rows and baseline latency curves. Happy to walk through the numbers in a 30-minute deep-dive.

— Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
